question.problem: Compute the gradient of the function $f: \mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/47c73d44f28380c2285b914445d6e4eed32e20e4304f8373b0e650d238497569.svg) with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/0648ff5db79fc2b00307e99fc1b14ddbc277982db84205f281f567a9c39b1eeb.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Writing ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220728/assets/f6bba4e49e37c8115f3d5696f3763224ae83da30fa92e295da8ae2905b6cfe9a.svg), we have

$$
f(\mathbf{x})= \mathbf{x}^TA\mathbf{x}.
$$

For a symmetric matrix $A$, the gradient of the function $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{x}^TA\mathbf{x}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is

$$
\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} f(\mathbf{x}) = 2A\mathbf{x}.
$$

Therefore, since $A$ is symmetric, we get
